title: Anna Karenina

scenesThatPass:
ANNA: Au revoir, Countess.
COUNTESS VRONSKY: Au revoir, my dear. Let me kiss your pretty face.

ANNA: Well, that's the end of that.
KITTY: Will you stay for the Bobrishchev's ball, Anna?
ANNA: Oh . . . I always feel dull at a ball.
KITTY: How can you ever be dull?

ANNA: I know why you want me to come. You want everyone to be there because you're sure it's going to be your night.
KITTY: How did you know?
ANNA: I know everything.
ANNA: Oh, to be your age again . . . surrounded by that blue mist, like mist on the mountains

KITTY: No, ask Anna.
ANNA: No . . . I don't . . .
ANNA: Come on then.

ANNA: Then, for Kitty's sake.
COUNTESS NORDSTON: You're not dancing the mazurka? I won't have it.

plot: In 1874 Imperial Russia, aristocratic Anna Karenina travels from Saint Petersburg to Moscow to save the marriage of her brother Prince Oblonsky, who had had a love affair with his housemaid. Anna Karenina and her husband, Count Alexei Karenin, have a son but a cold marriage. Anna meets cavalry officer Count Vronsky at the train station and there's a mutual attraction. Soon she learns that Vronsky will propose to Kitty, the younger sister of her sister-in-law Dolly. Anna satisfactorily resolves her brother's infidelity case, and Kitty invites her to stay for the ball. However, Anna and Vronsky attract too much negative attention from the conservative community by dancing together too often. They end up having a love affair that leads Anna Karenina to a tragic fate.
